fields.name: units
fields.label: Units on the PESCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the winter heater months can be as heavy as the summer.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed in the connection details of the PESCO bill. It sets the fixed charge; 5 kW and above is billed on ToU rates instead.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick only if the bill prints the protected category; one heater or AC month over the limit removes it.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in; pick the quarter of the billing month.

fields.name: qta_per_unit
fields.label: QTA from the bill (overrides the quarter)
fields.placeholder: Leave blank to use the quarter above
fields.hint: If your bill prints a QTA per unit that differs from the quarter's figure, or the quarter is not in the list, type it here; a credit is negative.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Monthly fuel price adjustment printed on the PESCO bill, positive or negative. Leave blank if unknown.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

answer: A PESCO home in Peshawar or elsewhere in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa using {{in.units|int}} units in a month as an unprotected consumer on a {{in.sanctioned_kw|int}} kW connection pays about {{out.total_rs|rs}}: {{out.energy_rs|rs}} energy charge at {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, the quarter's QTA and GST, before the month's FPA. PESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST.
how: {{out.units}} units × {{out.rate|rs2}} ({{out.category}} slab rate) = {{out.energy_rs|rs}}. Fixed charge for {{out.sanctioned_kw}} kW = {{out.fixed_rs|rs}}. FC surcharge {{out.fc_rs|rs}} + QTA {{out.qta_rs|rs}} + FPA {{out.fpa_rs|rs}}. Subtotal {{out.subtotal_rs|rs}} + GST {{out.gst_pct}}% ({{out.gst_rs|rs}}) = {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
key_facts: PESCO, the Peshawar Electric Supply Company, supplies the civil districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa from its head office in Peshawar and bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, the same slabs as every other ex-WAPDA DISCO.
An unprotected PESCO consumer using {{out.units|int}} units pays {{out.rate|rs2}} on every unit, which is {{out.energy_rs|rs}} of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.

The QTA changes by quarter: the same {{ex.1.out.units|int}} units come to about {{ex.1.out.total_rs|rs}} in the September to November quarter and about {{ex.2.out.total_rs|rs}} in the June to August quarter, when the adjustment was a credit.

A Khyber Pakhtunkhwa winter month of {{ex.3.out.units|int}} units with a fan heater and an electric geyser costs about {{ex.3.out.total_rs|rs}} unprotected, against about {{ex.0.out.total_rs|rs}} for a protected spring month of {{ex.0.out.units|int}} units.

Protection on PESCO needs every one of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} bills at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units on a connection below {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW; one heater month over the limit ends it for the next {{d.protected_months|int}} bills.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more; consumers on the list pay none.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC = financing cost surcharge; QTA = the quarter's tariff adjustment; FPA = the month's fuel price adjustment, all per unit from the PESCO bill

sections.h2: What is the PESCO per unit rate?
p: PESCO bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026; there is no separate PESCO tariff. An unprotected home in Peshawar, Mardan, Swat, Abbottabad, Bannu or Dera Ismail Khan pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: {{out.units|int}} units are all billed at {{out.rate|rs2}}. Protected consumers pay two low rates slab by slab, and lifeline consumers less again.

The table below prints the rate for each slab from the tariff file. The worked examples follow the same home through a protected spring month, the same units in two different quarters, a winter heater month and a lifeline bill.

sections.h2: PESCO tariff: why the QTA line changes every quarter
p: The quarterly tariff adjustment is a per-unit amount NEPRA sets for each three-month block to true up the DISCOs' costs, and it is applied to every unit of the month except on lifeline bills. It can be a charge or a credit. In the examples, {{ex.1.out.units|int}} units cost {{ex.1.out.total_rs|rs}} in the September to November quarter and {{ex.2.out.total_rs|rs}} in the June to August quarter, where the adjustment was a credit. Pick the quarter of the billing month under advanced settings, or type the QTA per unit from the bill if your quarter is not listed.
The FPA is separate: a monthly fuel price adjustment set after the month ends, so this page cannot know it in advance. Copy it from the bill into the FPA field; GST is charged on both lines.

sections.h2: Winter in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: heaters and geysers on the PESCO bill
p: Peshawar has cold winters and the hill districts colder ones, and when gas pressure falls electric heating takes over. A fan heater draws about {{a.room-heater-fan.running_w|int}} W, an oil-filled radiator about {{a.room-heater-oil-filled.running_w|int}} W and a storage geyser about {{a.electric-geyser-storage.running_w|int}} W, so a few hours a day of each adds hundreds of units. That is how a home protected in October reaches {{ex.3.out.units|int}} units in January and a bill of {{ex.3.out.total_rs|rs}}.

The lower districts such as Dera Ismail Khan and Bannu also have hot summers with AC loads, so some PESCO homes see two peaks a year. The home load calculator linked below adds up your heaters and ACs into units per month; enter that figure here.

sections.h2: PESCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the PESCO site
p: This PESCO bill estimate works from the units you type and does not fetch your account. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the PESCO website, which links the duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of any earlier bill there, digits only. Use the estimate to see what each printed line should be and to plan the winter months.
If the reading dates on the bill cover more than a month, the units may have been pushed into a higher slab by the long cycle; the bill audit tool linked below checks that for you.

mistakes: Looking for a PESCO tariff of its own. PESCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; the QTA and FPA lines are the parts that move from quarter to quarter and month to month.
Leaving the quarter on the default for an old bill. The QTA differs by quarter and can be a credit; pick the quarter of the billing month or type the figure from the bill.

Planning the winter on the autumn bill. A heater and a geyser can double or treble the units, and one month over {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units ends protected status for the next {{d.protected_months|int}} bills.
Dividing the bill total by units to find the PESCO per unit rate. Fixed charge, surcharges and GST are inside the total; the slab rate is the energy line divided by units.

faq.q: How do I get a PESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill prints that category, pick the billing quarter and add the FPA from the bill under advanced settings. For {{out.units|int}} units the estimate is {{out.total_rs|rs}} before FPA.

faq.q: What is the PESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: {{out.rate|rs2}} per unit for an unprotected home using {{out.units|int}} units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: Is the PESCO tariff different from the Punjab DISCOs?
faq.a: No. The 2026 tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026 is uniform for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. For the same units a PESCO bill differs from a LESCO or IESCO bill only by the month's FPA.

faq.q: What is the QTA on a PESCO bill?
faq.a: The quarterly tariff adjustment, a per-unit charge or credit NEPRA sets for each three-month block and applies to all units except lifeline. For {{out.units|int}} units in the default quarter it comes to {{out.qta_rs|rs}}; pick a different quarter or type the bill's figure to see another.

The civil districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, run from Peshawar through regional circles; the former tribal districts are served by TESCO. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator.

faq.q: How do I check my PESCO bill online?
faq.a: The PESCO website links a duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill, digits only, to see the current bill and due date. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Does a winter heater make a PESCO home unprotected?
faq.a: It can. Protection needs all of the last {{d.protected_months|int}} bills at or under {{d.protected_max_units|int}} units. A fan heater of about {{a.room-heater-fan.running_w|int}} W run a few hours a day adds well over a hundred units a month, enough to cross the limit on its own.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}}?
faq.a: A bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.
